items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: I heard Buddy, but I didn't know who he was.

ctx.x: But anyway, so you started taking lessons when you were about 18 years old. And then when did you start playing music?

Well then, I'll tell you what happened. I've forgotten about this. I returned in the Orleans in 1921. That's when I met Chester's artists. They were advertising. And I rode on the truck. While I'm still in the preliminary stages. So. You hadn't played any jobs yet. Well I played some with a little band, with Bernie Young, Al Simeon, Omar Simeon, Jimmy McHenry, and people like that, you know. And we were non-union. Just 15? Yeah, we were non-union then. items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1958-06-02
items.q: They said, oh man, we got Buddy P.T. and Randy A2.

ctx.x: Well when did you leave about?

In 1917. I arrived in Chicago January the 3rd, 1917. I was thirteen years old. And it wasn't long before I began to hear them talking about Louis Armstrong. My, at the time it was Joe Oliver. I'd seen them fellas bucking one another, him and Mutt. René, I hadn't heard of René. And I hadn't heard of Louis because I saw Louis.
